Opmv 1689/2018 Of Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-Iv, Ernakulam
Applicant/Appellant:
 Vidyasagar A.S., Aged 55 Years, S/O.Sivan, Amabalaparambil House,
 Opposite Petrol Pump, Thiruvankulam P.O., Ernakulam - 682305
Respondent/Respondent:
 National Insurance Company Limited, Regional Office, 1 And 2Nd
 Floor, Omana Building, Jews Street, Padma Junction, Ernakulam,
 Cochin - 682035
 Represented By Its Authorised Officer
 Application praying that in the circumstances stated in the
affidavit filed therewith the High Court be pleased to condone the delay
of 715 days caused in filing the above appeal, so as to secure the ends of
justice.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application
and the affidavit filed in support thereof, and upon hearing the arguments
of M/S. Rahul Sasi, Neethu Prem, Sruthy Saijo & V.A.Sandra, Advocates for
the applicant and Standing counsel for Respondent, the Court passed the
following:
 P.T.O
 C. Pratheep Kumar, J
 -----------------------------------------------

 in
 MACA.No.37 of 2025
 ------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 07th day of February, 2025
 Order
Vidyasagar A.S vs National Inssurance Company Limited on 7 February, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11273229/
1

This is an application filed by the appellant praying for condoning t
he delay of 715 days in filing the appeal.
2. The application was opposed on the ground that sufficient ground was not stated for condoning the delay.
3. The petitioner filed the above appeal claiming enhancement of compensation in respect of injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident.

Considering the fact that this appeal related to claim for compensation under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, I hold that the delay of 715 days in filing the appeal can be condoned on condition that the petitioner shall waive the interest for the enhanced amount of compensation awarded, if any, for the period of delay in filing the appeal.
4. In the result, this application is allowed on condition that the petitioner will not be eligible for interest for the enhanced amount of compensation, if any, in appeal.
The learned Standing Counsel takes notice for the respondent.
The learned counsel for the appellant is directed to serve a copy of the appeal memorandum to the learned Standing Counsel.
SMA /True Copy/ Assista Vidyasagar A.S vs National Inssurance Company Limited on 7 February, 2025
